title: VCe - Long Vowels with 'e'
source: Science of Reading Level 6 Teacher Guide

units.title: Introduction to Silent e
units.summary: Mini-lesson 1. Review: a closed syllable gives a short vowel (shop); a syllable that ends in a vowel can say its name (she). Silent e is the first job introduced: it tells the reader that another vowel will say its long sound. The silent e has many jobs: it makes vowels long, makes c say /s/ and g say /j/, keeps words from ending in v, keeps a word from looking plural, and gives the voiced th. Students review short vowels (apple, Eddie, igloo, otter, upstairs) and long vowels (apron, equal, iron, over, unicorn).

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Say a word and identify the vowel sound: like, late, cast, mole, mop, wave, cube, bike, build, mute, male; is it long?

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Closed syllables (shop) and open syllables (she); a vowel that says its name is a long vowel.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: The letter e can be silent; one job of the silent e is to make the other vowel long.

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles and label the vowel and consonants.

objectives.text: explain that a silent e makes the vowel before it say its name
tell short vowels in shop and cap from long vowels in she and cake
say what the silent e does in words like cake and bike
read one-syllable words that end in a vowel, like me, go and hi

replaces: Open Syllables · Y as a vowel (long i)

units.title: a_e
units.summary: Lesson 2: long a with the VCe pattern (cake, name, late). Compare with the short a words from Level 2; sort by word family or short versus long vowel. High-frequency words to map: made, make, take, came, gave, ate.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear the long a sound in spoken words and segment them into sounds.

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles; the first vowel says its name and the e is silent.

lessons.title: Encoding (spelling)
lessons.notes: Sound boxes: match each sound, then add the silent e.

lessons.title: Decoding (reading)
lessons.notes: Spot the VCe pattern, then read the word; short or long vowel?

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and write words from the word list; reading phrases and sentences; dictation.

lessons.title: "Mapping" high-frequency words
lessons.notes: made, make, take, came, gave, ate (the silent e can sit in the last box or outside the boxes)

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Word sorts by word family or short versus long vowel; student workbook pages.

objectives.text: read words like cake, name, late and game with a long a
spell words with the a_e pattern, such as safe, wave and shake
tell short a words from long a words, like cap and cape
read the common words made, make, take, came, gave and ate

units.title: o_e
units.summary: Lesson 4: long o with the VCe pattern (home, bone, nose). Some o_e words are very irregular, such as move; those are taught as heart words. High-frequency words: those, more, move.

objectives.text: read words like home, bone, rope and stone with a long o

units.title: u_e
units.summary: Lesson 5: long u with the VCe pattern. Long u has two sounds, /ū/ as in rule and /yū/ as in cube. Regular high-frequency word: use; irregular: sure.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear the long u sound in spoken words and segment them into sounds.

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles; the first vowel says its name and the e is silent.

lessons.title: Encoding (spelling)
lessons.notes: Sound boxes: match each sound, then add the silent e.

lessons.title: Decoding (reading)

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and write words from the word list; reading phrases and sentences; dictation.

lessons.title: "Mapping" high-frequency words
lessons.notes: use (regular), sure (irregular)

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Word sorts by word family or short versus long vowel; student workbook pages.

objectives.text: read words like cube, huge, tube and rule with a long u
spell words with the u_e pattern, such as mule, flute and fume
tell the two long u sounds in cube and rule
read the common words use and sure

units.title: Review: all vowels mixed
units.summary: Review of all four VCe patterns (a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e) together, to automaticity; duration varies. Word sorts by short or long vowel, reading phrases and connected text, and the word and sentence reading assessments. High-frequency words reviewed: make, take, made, came, gave, ate, five, like, here, time, white, ride, more, those, these, use, write; irregular: some, come, move, change, one, done.

lessons.title: Warm-up
lessons.notes: Read word endings and graphemes taught so far.

lessons.title: Mixed reading and spelling
lessons.notes: Words with all four VCe patterns; sort by vowel sound.

lessons.title: Reading phrases and sentences
lessons.notes: Model decoding each word, then reread.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: Regular and irregular lists.

lessons.title: Assessment
lessons.notes: Word reading and sentence reading; accuracy and fluency.

objectives.text: read and spell words that mix a_e, i_e, o_e and u_e
sort words by whether the vowel is long or short
read two-syllable words and compound words that contain a silent e, like cupcake and inside
write dictated sentences with long vowel words

units.title: -se and -ze
units.summary: Lesson 6. The /z/ sound at the end of a silent e word is usually spelled s (nose, use); z is less common. Use can say /yūs/ or /yūz/. Phonemic awareness, mapping and reading words with the final /z/ sound.

lessons.title: Model spelling
lessons.notes: Nose: /n/ /ō/ /z/; s spells /z/ and then add the silent e.

lessons.title: Reading words
lessons.notes: Point out the VCe pattern in nose, use and similar words.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Word lists, sentences and workbook pages.

objectives.text: hear /z/ at the end of words like nose and use
spell words that end in /z/ with a silent e, like rose and size
read words like these, those, prize and froze
know that use can be said two ways, as a noun and as a verb

units.title: -ce
units.summary: Lesson 7. Job 2 of silent e: when e follows c, the c says /s/ (ice, lace). This is one way to spell the /s/ sound at the end of silent e words, besides s (base, wise). High-frequency words: place, chance, once. Soft c: c says /s/ before e, i or y.

lessons.title: Introduce
lessons.notes: Build wise and base, then ice; the e makes c say /s/.

lessons.title: Model spelling
lessons.notes: Lace: /l/ /ā/ /s/ with sound boxes.

lessons.title: Lessons 7a and 7b
lessons.notes: Read and spell words that end in ce.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Reading words and sentences, spelling and dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: place, chance, once.

objectives.text: know that the silent e after c makes the c say /s/
read words like ice, lace, face and dance
spell words that end with the /s/ sound, such as place, price and fence
sort c words by the sound c makes, soft c before e, i or y

replaces: Multisyllable & Morphology · Soft c and Soft G

units.title: -ge and -dge
units.summary: Lessons 8a and 8b. Job 3 of silent e: after /j/ at the end of a word, use ge or dge, since j does not end English words. After a short vowel use dge (judge, ridge); after a long vowel or a consonant use ge (page, huge, plunge). ck, tch and dge are used only after short vowels. Words ending in -age and -ure are formed with the same silent e.

lessons.title: Lesson 8a: ge
lessons.notes: Model page and huge; the e makes the vowel long and the g say /j/ (two jobs).

lessons.title: Lesson 8b: dge
lessons.notes: Segment judge, page, ridge, singe, plunge; what comes right before /j/.

lessons.title: Spelling review
lessons.notes: ck, tch and dge are only used after short vowels.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Reading and spelling words with ge and dge; dictation.

objectives.text: choose dge after a short vowel and ge after a long vowel or a consonant
read words like page, huge, bridge and fudge
spell words that end in the /j/ sound, such as judge, stage and badge
read words that end in -age, such as cage and stage

units.title: -ve
units.summary: Lesson 9. Job 4 of silent e: English words do not end in v, so a word that ends with /v/ gets a silent e. After a short vowel the silent e does not make the vowel long: delve, give, have, live, solve, twelve, valve. Irregular: dove, love, move. Long vowel words: cave, cove, crave, dive, five, grove, hive, save, stove, wave. High-frequency words: have, give, live.

lessons.title: Warm-up
lessons.notes: Graphemes A to Z, sh, ch, th, tch, ng, ck, a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e, ce, ge, dge.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Segment twelve, give, cave, active.

lessons.title: Spelling review
lessons.notes: dge, tch, ck and floss words come only after short vowels.

lessons.title: Reading and spelling
lessons.notes: Long vowel -ve words and short vowel -ve words.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: have, give, live; irregular dove, love, move.

objectives.text: know that no English word ends in the letter v without a silent e
read long vowel words like cave, dive and wave
read short vowel words like give, have and live
spell words that end in /v/, such as glove, solve and drove

units.title: Suffix -s and -es with silent e
units.summary: Lesson 10. Adding -s or -es to a silent e word: if the word ends in /j/, /s/ or /z/ the suffix is -es and the e makes its own syllable (noses). Cover the suffix, read the base word first, then count syllables.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Suffix -s
lessons.notes: Read and spell silent e words plus -s (cakes, bikes).

lessons.title: Lesson 10b: Suffix -es
lessons.notes: Words ending in /j/, /s/ or /z/ take -es (noses); how many syllables?

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Reading and spelling, workbook pages.

objectives.text: read plurals and verbs like cakes, bikes and homes
explain why noses and prices need -es
add -s or -es to silent e words, such as faces and bridges

units.title: Suffixes -ed and -ing
units.summary: Lesson 11. A vowel suffix (starting with a vowel sound) means dropping the silent e from the base word: hope, hoped, hoping. With one consonant after the vowel the vowel is long; a doubled consonant shows a short vowel (hopping, hopped). Practice words: faked, making, smiled, waving, voted, muting. Dropping y rule: when a word ends in a consonant then y, change y to i before adding suffixes except -ing.

lessons.title: Review the dropping rule
lessons.notes: Hope, hoped, hoping.

lessons.title: Compare with doubling
lessons.notes: Hop, hopping, hopped.

lessons.title: Reading practice
lessons.notes: Faked, making, smiled, waving, voted, muting.

lessons.title: Spelling practice
lessons.notes: Add -ed and -ing to silent e words.

objectives.text: drop the silent e before adding -ed or -ing, as in hope, hoped, hoping
tell hoping from hopping by the number of consonants
spell words like making, smiled and waving
change y to i before adding a suffix, as in carry and carried

units.title: Plural-cancelling e
units.summary: Lesson 12 (mini-lesson). Another job of silent e: it shows the reader that a final s is part of the base word and not a plural suffix (dense, else, lapse, pulse, rinse, sense, tense). Not taught in depth; students meet more of these later with two-syllable words.

lessons.title: Build and compare
lessons.notes: Den and dens (plural) against dense; what the final e tells the reader.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell dense, else, lapse, pulse, rinse, sense, tense.

lessons.title: Workbook
lessons.notes: Two workbook pages.

objectives.text: tell a plural -s from an s that belongs to the word, as in dens and dense
read words like dense, else, pulse and sense
spell words like tense, rinse and lapse

units.title: Voiced th: -the
units.summary: Lesson 13 (mini-lesson). Another job of silent e: it shows that th is voiced (bathe, clothe). Words to use now: bathe, clothe. After the lessons: give the word and sentence reading assessments; if students are accurate but slow, give more practice with decodable text rather than reteaching.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: The silent e after th makes the voiced sound: bath and bathe.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell bathe and clothe.

lessons.title: After the lessons
lessons.notes: Word and sentence reading assessment; extra decodable text for fluency.

objectives.text: hear that the th in bathe is voiced and the th in bath is not
read bathe and clothe
spell words that end in -the, such as breathe

units.title: Review of all silent e
units.summary: End of the unit. Review all jobs of silent e: long vowels (VCe), ce, ge, dge, ve, se and ze, plural-cancelling e, voiced th. Reading and spelling assessments with word, phrase and sentence lists; student workbook review pages.
